projects.title: Third-Person Soulslike Combat Prototype
projects.role: Gameplay & Combat Design / Blueprint Systems / Animation Retargeting
projects.summary: A third-person action prototype built entirely in Unreal Blueprint. It explores attack and dodge flow, hit feedback, projectile behavior, input response, and gameplay tuning while using interfaces, Actor Components, and base classes to create an extensible modular structure.
projects.tools: Unreal Engine 5, Blueprint, Animation Montage, AnimNotifyState, Blueprint Interface, Actor Component, Data Asset

detail.overview: This third-person action prototype was created entirely in Unreal Blueprint with no C++. It tests attack, dodge, hit detection, enemy feedback, and projectile behavior while practicing maintainable system organization through EnemyBase, ProjectileBase, Actor Components, Blueprint Interfaces, and component tags.
whatIBuilt: Implemented light and heavy attacks, dodge, stamina, lock-on, hit detection, damage, and enemy reactions.
Implemented projectile spawning, collision, valid-target checks, and cleanup.
Used AnimNotifyState to control active hit frames for different melee weapons and align impacts with damage numbers and feedback.
Worked on input buffering and animation-state transitions to reduce sticky controls and state conflicts during rapid combat.
Retargeted animation assets and connected animation, audio, VFX, and UI to combat events.
Used exposed parameters, Data Assets, and visual debug traces to support rapid gameplay tuning.

breakdown.label: Modular Communication
breakdown.text: Extracted EnemyBase and ProjectileBase, moved reusable logic into Actor Components, and used Blueprint Interfaces and component tags to reduce direct references.

breakdown.label: Animation & Hit Frames
breakdown.text: Used AnimNotifyState to define active frames so collision, damage, reaction, and UI feedback match the visible animation.

breakdown.label: Input & State Flow
breakdown.text: Organized input buffering and animation-state transitions to reduce conflicts between attacks, dodges, and reactions.

breakdown.label: Data-Driven Debugging
breakdown.text: Exposed damage, cooldown, and timing parameters and used Draw Debug traces to calibrate attack ranges and invulnerability frames.

challenges: Weapon animation and active hit frames had to match precisely or the visual impact and actual damage would feel disconnected.
Rapid inputs exposed conflicts between buffering, animation states, and combat-state resets.
As the prototype expanded, direct casts and Actor references became expensive to maintain, making modularity and low coupling a design requirement.
detail.workflowNotes: I iterated in PIE with data-driven parameters and visual debugging for damage, cooldowns, attack windows, and dodge invulnerability. AI tools supported research and troubleshooting; the final Blueprint structure, implementation, and validation were completed in Unreal Engine.

projects.title: Punk Plush Panic
projects.category: Unity · Capstone · 2.5D Action Platformer · Team Project
projects.role: Combat Design / Level Design / VFX / Systems Design
projects.summary: A fast-paced 2.5D action platformer where players swap between three characters and combine their abilities against enemy waves. I contributed combat and systems design, level iteration, VFX, boss timing, and attack readability improvements.
projects.tools: Unity, Level Design, Boss Design, VFX, Playtest Feedback, Cross-Discipline Collaboration

detail.overview: Punk Plush Panic is my capstone project, built by a multidisciplinary team. Players swap between three characters and combine their abilities against waves of enemies. My work focused on combat and systems design, level and encounter iteration, VFX feedback, playtest analysis, and communication with programmers around boss readability.
whatIBuilt: Contributed to gameplay systems, combat rules, level spaces, and encounter iteration.
Adjusted player routes, enemy pressure, and opportunities for character swapping.
Reduced level scope late in production to protect the core experience and help the team ship on time.
Collected playtest feedback, organized issues, and helped the team select actionable changes.
Retuned boss ability timing and coordinated the addition of ground telegraphs with programmers.
Created smoke, wind, and early skill and buff VFX; some early effects were replaced during later visual iteration.

breakdown.label: Boss Telegraphing
breakdown.text: Retuned release timing and coordinated ground indicators so players could read attack range and react fairly.

breakdown.label: Scope Management
breakdown.text: Evaluated level priorities and cut lower-value content when time became limited, protecting the core flow and team delivery.

breakdown.label: Playtesting & Iteration
breakdown.text: Collected feedback, categorized experience problems, and discussed implementation cost and value with the team.

breakdown.label: VFX Feedback
breakdown.text: Created environmental and early gameplay effects that communicated mood, abilities, and state changes while helping define later visual requirements.

challenges: Boss attacks initially lacked enough warning for players to understand their range or failure state.
Late-production constraints required balancing the original level vision against a reliable delivery scope.
Some early VFX were later replaced, so their portfolio value is framed as feedback prototyping and direction-setting rather than final-art ownership.
detail.workflowNotes: My workflow combined identifying player-experience problems, proposing solutions, coordinating implementation, gathering playtest feedback, and iterating with the team. The boss telegraph and level-scope decisions demonstrate both experience design and production judgment.

projects.title: Breach Brew
projects.category: Commercial Project · Unreal Engine · Environmental Gameplay Systems
projects.role: Technical Design / Technical Art / Gameplay Systems Implementation
projects.summary: Designed and implemented an event-driven environmental temperature system that drives gameplay state, material parameters, and Niagara VFX while improving the readability of environmental mechanics.
projects.tools: Unreal Engine, Blueprint, Material Parameters, Niagara, Environmental Interaction, Cross-Discipline Collaboration

detail.overview: Breach Brew is a commercial game project where I contributed to an environmental temperature system that connects gameplay state, material response, and Niagara VFX. I collaborated with technical artists and designers to integrate the system in-engine.
whatIBuilt: Designed and implemented an event-driven temperature system in Blueprint.
Created gameplay-responsive material parameters for heat and cold transitions.
Connected Niagara VFX to environmental and gameplay events.
Built interactive environmental mechanics and improved gameplay readability.
Collaborated with technical artists and designers to integrate systems and visual feedback.

breakdown.label: Temperature State
breakdown.text: Used shared state and events to update environmental temperature rather than running complex independent logic on every object.

breakdown.label: Material Response
breakdown.text: Drove heat and cold transitions through parameters so visual state responds smoothly to gameplay data.

breakdown.label: Niagara Feedback
breakdown.text: Connected VFX to environmental events so players can quickly read temperature and danger changes.

breakdown.label: Cross-Discipline Integration
breakdown.text: Separated system interfaces and visual responsibilities so design and technical art could iterate independently.

challenges: Gameplay logic, materials, and VFX needed one consistent data source to avoid visible state drifting from actual system state.
Public project images and video have not been uploaded yet, so this preview uses media placeholders.

projects.title: The E Book
projects.category: Commercial Project · Unity · Gameplay Data & Tooling
projects.role: Gameplay Data Configuration / Workflow Design / AI-Assisted Tool Development
projects.summary: Maintained complex gameplay-balancing spreadsheets, redesigned the data workflow, and used AI-assisted development to create a utility that converts designer-friendly Excel sheets into Unity-ready configuration data.
projects.tools: Excel, Unity, Basic Python, AI-Assisted Development, Data Validation

detail.overview: On The E Book, I maintained gameplay data configurations and restructured Excel sheets so designers could edit data more efficiently. I then used an AI-assisted workflow to develop a utility that converts the spreadsheets into a Unity-readable configuration format.
whatIBuilt: Created and maintained complex gameplay-balancing spreadsheets.
Redesigned spreadsheet structure for clearer editing and batch tuning.
Developed an AI-assisted Excel-to-Unity conversion utility.
Reduced manual formatting work and data-entry errors.
Worked with designers to validate the workflow against real balancing needs.

breakdown.label: Designer-Friendly Input
breakdown.text: Allowed designers to work in readable spreadsheets instead of engine-facing data formats.

breakdown.label: Automated Conversion
breakdown.text: Converted Excel data into a Unity-readable format and reduced repeated manual work.

breakdown.label: Error Control
breakdown.text: Used structural constraints and validation to reduce missing fields and format mismatches.

breakdown.label: Iteration Speed
breakdown.text: Shortened the path between data edits and in-engine testing.

challenges: The spreadsheet had to remain readable for designers while structured enough for reliable automation.
Public portfolio assets must use anonymized or fictional data to avoid exposing commercial information.

Adjusted interaction distance, response, and handling based on headset testing.
Built portions of the level and environment.
Created and tuned glass, water, and other environmental materials.

breakdown.label: Puzzle Logic

breakdown.label: Door & State Logic
breakdown.text: Handled conditions, open/closed states, and interaction feedback.
